newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN PLASTIC PROCESSORS HAD LOWER 1996 TURNOVER.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN PLASTIC PROCESSORS HAD LOWER 1996 TURNOVER.

text.p: Turnover in the Belgian plastics processing industry fell by one percent in 1996 from 1995, the industry's umbrella organisation said on Tuesday.
A recovery in demand in the final quarter of 1996 helped the industry recover from a 5.5 percent fall in turnover in the first half, the organisation said in a statement.

Margins were hit by a rise in raw materials prices from the low levels of 1995. PVC prices rose by 30 percent and prices of polyethylene and polypropylene by almost 50 percent in the course of the year.

Margins also suffered from a trend towards concentration in the distribution sector, which resulted in increasing purchasing power in the car, consumer goods, construction, furniture and do-it-yourself business.
The industry was threatened by displacements, not necessarily of producers, but of its clients.

Recent examples included the furniture industry, which moved to low-cost eastern European countries, and French car maker Renault which has decided to move car assembly from Belgium to France and Spain to cut overcapacity.
